title: Handshake telemetry timeline and config notebook
body:
Purpose
This is a personal working notebook to capture a compact, end-to-end picture of the client-server handshake telemetry we want to collect during session establishment and resume. Aim is to converge on an API shape + sampling rules + retention TTLs that are lightweight (mobile/edge friendly) and useful for diagnosing resume failures, routing decisions and cost-aware fallback.

High-level goals (constraints)
- Keep per-handshake payload <= 1KB typical (rarely > 2KB) for mobile clients.
- Telemetry should not contain user PII or prompt text. Only hashed IDs or truncated intent signals.
- Provide enough events to reconstruct timeline of resume attempts and fallbacks (region switch, model variant fallback).
- Allow deterministic linking to a server-side trace ID for deep-dive when available.
- Support adaptive sampling: full traces for failures, downsample routine success handshakes.

Event timeline (sequence)
1) CLIENT: handshake:init -> client sends minimal capabilities and session token (opaque).
   fields: client_ts, client_id_hash, client_version, region_hint, capabilities_mask
2) SERVER: handshake:ack -> server assigns ephemeral session_id, route decision (hosted/dedicated), chosen_model_variant (id+qualifier), server_ts, trace_id (nullable).
3) CLIENT: prefetch:kv-probe (optional) -> quick kv cache probe (hashes only) to decide prefix cache hit.
4) SERVER: resume:attempt -> server returns resume_result { success|stale|partial|fallback }, latency_ms, selected_fallback_reason (if any).
5) CLIENT: streaming:start (if success) -> streaming tokens begin; telemetry samples token latency separately.
6) SERVER: session:handoff/finalize -> final state (pinned_model_version, kv_snapshot_id) or error.

ASCII timeline example:
[client 09:12:03.123] handshake:init -> {cap_mask=0x12, region=us-west}
    [server 09:12:03.187] handshake:ack -> {session_id=ephemeral-42, variant=xq-8}
    [client 09:12:03.190] prefetch:kv-probe -> {kv_probe=3 hashes}
    [server 09:12:03.210] resume:attempt -> {result=partial, missing_prefix=true, fallback=model-smaller}
    [client 09:12:03.215] streaming:start -> {first_chunk_ts=09:12:03.216}

Minimal API shape (telemetry envelope)
- This is intentionally compact. Use snake_case for fields.

telemetry_envelope = {
  "version": "v1",                              // string
  "client_ts": "2026-02-15T09:12:03.123Z",     // string (ISO)
  "client_id_hash": "sha256:abcd...",         // string
  "session_token_hash": "sha256:efgh...",     // string (opaque hashed token)
  "session_id": "ephemeral-42",               // string (filled after ack)
  "events": [                                   // list of compact event objects
    "handshake:init|client_version=1.4.2|cap=0x12|region=us-west|ts=2026-02-15T09:12:03.123Z",
    "handshake:ack|session_id=ephemeral-42|variant=xq-8|route=hosted|server_ts=2026-02-15T09:12:03.187Z"
  ],
  "outcome": "partial|fallback=model-smaller", // string (summary)
  "latency_ms": "87",                          // string (aggregate ms)
  "trace_id": "optional-trace-999",           // string (only when available)
  "sample_rate": "0.02"                       // string (float as string to avoid nested types)
}

Notes on the events array format:
- Storing events as compact pipe-delimited strings keeps JSON envelope smaller and parsing cheap on ingestion side. The ingestion pipeline will split on '|' and index top-level tags.
- Allowed event types: handshake:init, handshake:ack, prefetch:kv-probe, resume:attempt, streaming:start, session:finalize, error.
- We deliberately avoid storing prompt_text or embedding vectors. Put only hashed or categorical signals (e.g., intent_tag=reply).

Resume result taxonomy (server-side canonical strings)
- success
- partial -> resumed but missing some prefix context (server will do conservative continuation)
- stale -> cached context too old; full re-sync required
- fallback -> resumed but chose smaller model or region fallback
- error -> auth failure / corrupted token

Adaptive sampling rules (proposal)
- If outcome != success: sample 100% (we need full traces for failures).
- If outcome == success: sample at dynamic rate = base_rate * exp(-q) where q = recent failure_rate_in_1h_bucket * 50 (capped). Default base_rate = 0.02 (2%).
- For VIP customers (dedicated/enterprise flag in handshake:ack route), always sample at least 0.1 (10%).
- Periodically (daily) run targeted bursts: for each region-model pair pick 50 random successful handshakes for quality sampling and model drift checks.

Privacy & retention
- Do not store user prompt text. If in debug mode only, store prompt hashes (sha256) and strip salt on request from privacy team.
- Keep raw handshake envelopes and full traces for 30 days by default. Aggregated counters (failure rates per region/model) retained 1 year.
- Provide customer toggles: opt-out telemetry (returns anonymized counters only) and opt-in full traces via enterprise contract.

Config knobs (server-side, example keys)
- telemetry.enabled: bool (true)
- telemetry.base_sample_rate: float (0.02)
- telemetry.vip_min_rate: float (0.1)
- telemetry.min_payload_retention_days: int (30)
- telemetry.aggregate_retention_days: int (365)
- telemetry.failure_sampling: {always: true}
- handshake.max_payload_bytes: int (2048)
- handshake.reject_if_no_hash: bool (true)  // reject if client sent PII-like fields un-hashed

Operational playbook snippets
- If sudden spike in resume:failure in a region -> ramp sample_rate to 100% for that region-model pair for 30 minutes; collect traces and look for common fallback reasons.
- If trace_id present in handshake:ack and the client reports a resume failure, do cross-linking by trace_id and mark incidents with link to the trace.
- When investigating QoS regressions, prioritize samples where resume:attempt.result==partial and latency_ms > 200ms.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-ups)
- How to signal user-level debug mode securely without leaking PII? Proposal: client sends debug_cap_nonce signed by customer key; allow full prompt hashes for duration-limited sessions only.
- Should we include a small sketch of token-acceptance histogram in the envelope? (adds size but could help diagnose slow-tail tokenization).
- Schema evolution: design v2 to allow optional JSON blobs for vendor-specific telemetry but keep top-level indexable fields stable.
- Need a tiny server-side library (Go/TS) to pack events into the compact pipe-delimited format and enforce size limits.

Quick sample (realistic compact envelope stringified):
{
  \"version\": \"v1\",
  \"client_ts\": \"2026-02-15T09:12:03.123Z\",
  \"client_id_hash\": \"sha256:1a2b3c\",
  \"session_token_hash\": \"sha256:7e8f9a\",
  \"session_id\": \"ephemeral-42\",
  \"events\": [
    \"handshake:init|client_version=1.4.2|cap=0x12|region=us-west|ts=2026-02-15T09:12:03.123Z\",
    \"handshake:ack|session_id=ephemeral-42|variant=xq-8|route=hosted|server_ts=2026-02-15T09:12:03.187Z\",
    \"resume:attempt|result=partial|missing_prefix=true|latency_ms=23\"
  ],
  \"outcome\": \"partial|fallback=model-smaller\",
  \"latency_ms\": \"87\",
  \"trace_id\": \"tr-999\",
  \"sample_rate\": \"0.02\"
}

Notes to self: next steps
- Share this notebook with Arjun and Luis, iterate the event list and finalize canonical resume reasons.
- Prototype the client packer (TS) and server unpacker (Go) as a small PR in serving-runtime.
- Add a Confluence page that maps telemetry fields to elasticsearch indices and retention lifecycle for infra.

End of notebook (temporary working file).
